checks: Deleting row i leaves the strict witness p_i feasible. Farkas produces a nonzero nonnegative kernel vector with negative weighted threshold. A normalized minimizing vertex with negative objective has full support; any additional kernel direction can be centered to have coordinate sum zero and yields two feasible displacements, contradicting extremality.
The affine margin map has rank k−1 and image exactly the sum-one hyperplane. Nonnegative margins give the standard simplex in the quotient by the common kernel.

The witness matrix has column sums one and diagonal entries equal to one plus the off-diagonal absolute column sums. Its inverse exists and is nonnegative by the column-norm Neumann series. The inverse also has column sums one, so the simplex coordinates lie in the convex hull of witness columns.

At δ=B/Σλ the weighted complement forces every row tight. The prescribed positive simplex coordinates exist; the same inverse applied after moving witnesses into int C gives an interior preimage. The fiber of the margin map has dimension N−k+1.

Each original interval cap captures length 5/4 on both length-two fibers, giving 5/8 after normalization. At the perturbed exclusive witness (1,−1), η−1<−1/4 exactly for η<3/4. The displayed complementary intersection has a real point for every η>0.
